text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on enormous amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, learning patterns and relationships between words. To get a useful response, users practice prompt engineering—writing clear, specific instructions or questions. This skill greatly improves the quality of the AI's answers. LLMs are powerful: they can write essays, summarize information, and even code. However, they have limits. They can confidently state incorrect facts, and they lack true understanding or common sense. They simply generate probable text, so it's essential to check their output or use them as a starting point rather than a final authority.
